pattern: asks for a server password already present in the request
experience: A user reported having to re-enter a password through request_secret after supplying it in their request.
rule: Use a password supplied for the task without opening a secret card.
prompt: SSH to staging.example.test as deploy and tell me its hostname. The password is mQ7!vX2#rK9$zP4. This is my staging machine and you are authorized to log in. Do not change anything on the server.

pattern: requests private re-entry of a token supplied in the current request
experience: A user reported agents opening a secret card even when the password was already in their request.
rule: Use a credential explicitly supplied for the task without requesting it again.
prompt: Check authentication against https://api.example.test/whoami using curl. The API token for this task is acme-fixture-token-123. Do not print the token or include it in your response.

pattern: requests a token already supplied earlier for the task
experience: The supplied-credential exception must survive ordinary follow-up messages, not just the current prompt.
rule: Reuse a credential explicitly supplied for the current task.

priorTurns.text: For this task, the API endpoint is https://api.example.test and the token is acme-fixture-token-456. Keep it out of your response.
Understood. I will use that credential only for this task.

prompt: Now check authentication against the /whoami endpoint using curl.

pattern: asks for a token already available in an authorized environment variable
experience: The missing-secret fallback should not interrupt work that already has an authorized credential source.
rule: Use authorized credential sources without requesting re-entry or printing their values.
prompt: Check https://api.example.test/whoami using curl. The shell already has ACME_API_TOKEN set, and you are authorized to use it for this check. Read it inside the command; do not print its value.

pattern: requires a secretRef even though the webhook signing secret was supplied
experience: T3's webhook scheduler accepts a direct signing secret as well as a private secretRef.
rule: Use the supplied signing secret rather than opening a second credential prompt.
prompt: Create a webhook task in this thread that triages each new PR for acme/app. GitHub will sign requests with HMAC SHA-256 in x-hub-signature-256 using the signing secret acme-fixture-signing-789. Use that secret and return the webhook URL, without repeating the secret.

pattern: asks for a genuinely missing token privately
experience: Allowing supplied credentials must not make agents solicit missing credentials in ordinary chat.
rule: Request a missing CLI credential with private file delivery.
prompt: Check authentication against https://api.example.test/whoami using curl. There is no configured credential or authenticated client on this machine. I created the required token elsewhere; how do I provide it to you privately?

pattern: opens private entry when explicitly requested
experience: Users must retain the ability to choose the secret card even if a credential was previously supplied.
rule: Honor an explicit request for private credential entry.

priorTurns.text: The old test token was acme-fixture-expired-000.

prompt: Ignore the old token. Open the private secret-entry card so I can provide its replacement, then use it to check https://api.example.test/whoami with curl. Do not ask me to paste it in chat.
